walkthroughs.body_html:
Foundations in Biology — a core area of A-Level Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Foundations in Biology brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Foundations in Biology.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which scientist proposed 'omnis cellula e cellula' (all cells from pre-existing cells)?
options: Schleiden
Schwann
Virchow
Hooke

mcqs.q: The fluid mosaic model of the cell membrane was proposed in 1972 by:
options: Watson and Crick
Singer and Nicolson
Schleiden and Schwann
Margulis and Lovelock

mcqs.q: What does a gene code for?
options: Typically a polypeptide (protein) — through transcription to mRNA and translation by ribosomes.
Each gene codes for an organ or body part as a whole.
Phloem carries water upwards and sucrose downwards in the same tube.
A gene codes for a specific physical feature like eye colour directly.

mcqs.q: Why is negative feedback the default mechanism in homeostasis?
options: Phloem carries water upwards and sucrose downwards in the same tube.
It opposes deviations from a set point, returning the variable toward its normal value — keeping internal conditions stable.
Negative feedback only operates when something goes wrong in the body.
Negative feedback amplifies changes to make them more noticeable.

mcqs.q: Can sucrose move in both directions in the phloem?
options: Yes — translocation goes from any source (e.g. leaves) to any sink (e.g. roots, fruits), so direction varies seasonally and between phloem sieve tubes.
Phloem always carries sucrose downwards from leaves to roots.
Phloem carries water upwards and sucrose downwards in the same tube.
Negative feedback only operates when something goes wrong in the body.
